timeline.current_model: ROR1 is a transmembrane receptor tyrosine kinase (classified as a pseudokinase lacking intrinsic catalytic activity) that acts as a Wnt5a (and IGFBP5) receptor, signaling through Wnt5a-induced hetero-oligomerization with ROR2, recruitment of GEFs (DOCK2) via its cytoplasmic proline-rich domain, and activation of Rac1/RhoA and ERK1/2 to promote cancer cell proliferation and migration; it also phosphorylates HER3 at Tyr1307 (a kinase-independent-of-ErbB mechanism) to engage the MAYA/NSUN6-MST1/YAP axis for bone metastasis, and functions as a scaffold for cavin-1, CAV1, and CAVIN3 to maintain caveolae integrity and sustain multi-RTK pro-survival AKT signaling; its stability is maintained by HSP90α and its surface expression requires N-linked glycosylation, while it can complex with TCL1 to amplify AKT-driven leukemogenesis.
